LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterAllianceText: The Empire on this world recognizes {0} as its legitimate authority.\n\nEvery Imperial city is already an ally. Ordinary goodwill decay toward the Empire is suspended while a living colonist holds Emperor, Special Consul, or a recognized claim.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterHuntStartText: {0} bears the Hunted Assassin mark. Survive sixty days of succession crisis — frequent raids, hunters, rival claimants — and Imperial custom will recognize the claim on the throne.\n\nIf a Knight or higher kills the Marked One, the nanites jump and a fresh sixty days begin. You keep what you kill; you do not keep their leftover time.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterCrownText: The Hunted Assassin mark has burned out of {0}. Imperial custom recognizes the claim.\n\n{0} is crowned Emperor. The hunt is over. Play continues — hold the planet, keep the court alive, expand the Empire.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterInheritText:
{0} has slain the Marked One ({1}).

The Hunted Assassin subspace trackers leapt to their new host — as with every such mark, you keep what you kill.

A fresh sixty-day hunt begins. Each new claimant starts their own race for the throne.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterVassalText: {0} has been taken in the Empire's name. A Knight was present at victory, so the city remains as an Imperial vassal instead of a ruin.\n\nLoan a Knight to occupy it. A gap in Knight presence will break occupation. After five RimWorld years of continuous occupation, an Archon may convert it into an Imperial city.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterNoKnightText: {0} fell, but no colony Knight was present. The usual destruction follows — annexation requires a Knight or higher on the map when the last defenders break.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterRebellionText: {0} is no longer occupied. Without a Knight on site the vassal has rebelled, and the five-year clock is reset.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterLoanText: {0} has been loaned to {1} for sixty days. They cannot work the home colony during the term. Renew before expiry to keep occupation continuous.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterLoanEndedText: The loan of {0} at {1} has ended. Send or renew a Knight or occupation will break.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_LetterConvertedText: {0} has been converted. After five years of occupation, {1} performed the rite and the settlement is now an Imperial city — the same as the ones allied at the start.\n\nThe Archon may be recalled to the colony, or left as the city's governor.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_GizmoLoanDesc: Station a colony Knight at this vassal for sixty days. One Knight cannot occupy two vassals at once.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_GizmoRenewDesc: Extend the current Knight's term by another sixty days so occupation stays continuous.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_GizmoRecallKnightDesc: End the current term and drop the Knight back at the home colony. Occupation will break unless another Knight is already here or an Archon has converted the city.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_GizmoConvertDesc: An Archon in this caravan performs the conversion. The settlement joins the Empire faction.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_GizmoRecallArchonDesc: The Archon rejoins the colony as a colonist, title intact.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_NoKnightToLoan: No idle colony Knight is available to loan.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_ConvertNeedArchon: An Archon (or Count) in this caravan is required, and the vassal must have five years of continuous occupation.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_AnnexationDisabled: Emperors and Consuls: annexation disabled because another annexation mod is loaded ({0}).
LanguageData.BR_EAC_AlertNeedsKnightDesc: These Imperial vassals have no Knight on loan. Occupation will break (or already has a short grace after a death). Loan a Knight to keep the five-year clock.\n\n{0}
LanguageData.BR_EAC_InspectConvertedNoGovernor: Imperial city (converted). Recall remains available if a governor was left here.
LanguageData.BR_EAC_HuntRaidLetterText: Hunters and rival claimants have found the Marked One. The succession crisis does not wait.
